classification.difficultyReason: Use the supplied auxiliary-angle identity to sketch a shifted sine curve, then read the strict inequality between its intersections with y=1.

answer.worked:
Write $\sin x-\cos x=R\sin(x-\alpha)$, with $R>0$.
$$\begin{aligned}R\sin(x-\alpha)&=R\sin x\cos\alpha-R\cos x\sin\alpha.\end{aligned}$$
Comparing coefficients gives $R\cos\alpha=1$ and $R\sin\alpha=1$.
$$\begin{aligned}R^2\cos^2\alpha+R^2\sin^2\alpha&=1^2+1^2\\R^2&=2\\R&=\sqrt{2},\\\tan\alpha&=1.\end{aligned}$$
Both $\sin\alpha$ and $\cos\alpha$ are positive, so choose $\alpha=\frac{\pi}{4}$ in quadrant I.
$$\begin{aligned}\sin x-\cos x&=\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right).\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Hence sketch the graph of $y=\sin x-\cos x$, for $0\leq x\leq2\pi$.

answer.short: A sine curve of amplitude $\sqrt{2}$ and period $2\pi$, shifted right by $\frac{\pi}{4}$; see graph.
answer.worked: $y=\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ has amplitude $\sqrt{2}$ and period $2\pi$. It passes through $(0,-1)$, $\left(\frac{\pi}{4},0\right)$, $\left(\frac{3\pi}{4},\sqrt{2}\right)$, $\left(\frac{5\pi}{4},0\right)$, $\left(\frac{7\pi}{4},-\sqrt{2}\right)$ and $(2\pi,-1)$. The reference line $y=1$ meets the curve at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\pi$.

spec.description: Arrowed axes, quarter-pi ticks, labelled half-pi intervals, sine curve and dashed y=1 reference line. Endpoint label corrected to 2π. House style uses black ordinary axes and labels and standard blue for the function and reference line.
spec.mathematics: y=sin x-cos x=sqrt(2)sin(x-pi/4), 0<=x<=2pi; maximum sqrt(2), minimum -sqrt(2); y=1 at pi/2 and pi.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Use your sketch to determine the values of $x$ in the domain $0\leq x\leq2\pi$ for which
$$\sin x-\cos x>1.$$

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)&>1\\\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)&>\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}.\end{aligned}$$
The sketch lies above $y=1$ between its intersections at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $x=\pi$. Hence $\frac{\pi}{2}<x<\pi$; the endpoints are excluded because the inequality is strict.
